newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Morgan silent on reports ATN funded trip.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Morgan silent on reports ATN funded trip.

text.p: New Zealand First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan on Tuesday refused to comment on a newspaper report that he travelled to Europe at the expense of Aotearoa Television Network four days after being elected to Parliament.
The Dominion newspaper reported the Te Tai Hauauru MP's business class travel, accommodation at the Waldorf Meridien in London and other expenses cost the television station $11,739.

Morgan told reporters before his party's weekly caucus meeting that he had discussed the story with his legal counsel and had been advised to make no comment on matters affecting his reputation and integrity, NZPA reported.
"It is highly inappropriate for me to make any comment until the High Court case," he said.
Morgan is suing Labour MP Trevor Mallard for defamation over comments about his links with ATN.

Morgan, a former director and presenter at ATN, has been under fire since revelations last year he spent the cash- strapped station's money on expensive clothes only weeks before he was elected to parliament.

Fellow NZ First MP Tutekawa Wyllie told reporters he was not concerned about the newspaper report because Morgan had already briefed caucus about the trip, while party whip Ron Mark described the report as "old news".
NZ First leader, Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters, would not comment as he entered the meeting.
